summary: An ICCBased space whose profile this reader cannot apply and which states no /Alternate is parsed as the bare device space /N implies (DeviceGray, DeviceRGB or DeviceCMYK), so it stops being an ICCBased space for every question the clauses ask of the selected space. Two follow: §8.6.8's initial colour is the device family's rather than the ICCBased one's — /N 4 gives [0 0 0 1], black, where an ICCBased space starts at all-zero (no ink, white) and the same stream with /Alternate /DeviceCMYK does — and Table 65's /Range is not applied before the alternate: /N 1 /Range [0 0.5] with 0.8 sc draws grey 204 where the stated-/Alternate route (ADR 2973, 2038-B25) draws 128. The ADR 2973 construction (ColourSpace::IccAlternate) covers only the route where /Alternate is stated.
source: ISO 32000-2 Table 65, /Alternate: "If this entry is omitted and the PDF reader does not understand the ICC profile data, the colour space that shall be used is DeviceGray , DeviceRGB , or DeviceCMYK , depending on whether the value of N is 1 , 3 , or 4 , respectively. … Colour values within the range of the ICCBased colour space might not be within the range of the alternate colour space. In this case and after constraining to the ICCBased range, the nearest values within the range of the alternate space shall be substituted without error indication." §8.6.8: "In a Lab or ICCBased colour space, the initial colour shall have all components equal to 0.0 un less that falls outside the intervals specified by the space's Range entry".

summary: A Pattern space read where it carries no colour is drawn as opaque black and the page reports itself complete. ColourSpace::Pattern { base: None } counts one component and converts to Color::BLACK, so three routes paint a colour no clause gives: a shading whose /ColorSpace is /Pattern (Table 77 excludes it; the 8.7.4.3 ledger row says it is refused), an Indexed space whose base is /Pattern (§8.6.6.3 excludes it), and a bare number given to scn in a /Pattern space (§8.6.8's operand there is a pattern name), which fills black where the initial pattern paints nothing.
source: ISO 32000-2 §8.7.1: "These spaces shall use pattern objects as the equivalent of colour values instead of the numeric component values used with other spaces." Table 77, /ColorSpace: "This may be any colour space except a Pattern space." §8.6.6.3: "It shall be any device or CIE-based colour space or ( PDF 1.3 ) a Separation or DeviceN space, but shall not be a Pattern space or another Indexed space." §8.6.8: "If the current stroking colour space is a Pattern colour space, name shall be the name of an entry in the Pattern subdictionary of the current resource dictionary".

summary: The comment over /UseBlackPtComp in apply_ext_gstate says /BG, /BG2, /UCR and /UCR2 'are §10.4's, which this device does not perform, and are read for a flag and never evaluated'. They are evaluated: BlackGeneration::separate converts DeviceRGB into a DeviceCMYK group (§11.7.5.3, black_generation_transfer_audit), which is why B01 is visible. The sentence is the reason the entries were left outside the uncoloured guard.
source: ISO 32000-2 §10.4.2.4 and §11.7.5.3 (the pair controls a conversion into a DeviceCMYK blending space).
